projects.title: Endpoint Security & Activity Monitoring
projects.status: Built · verified end to end on Windows
projects.context: Law-firm product, designed to be sold multi-tenant
projects.desc: Cross-platform endpoint monitoring for company-managed devices — native Rust agents for Windows, macOS and Linux, a multi-tenant central server, org-encrypted screenshots and exfiltration alerts.
projects.overview: A multi-tenant activity-monitoring product for company-owned devices. A native agent runs as a normal, discoverable service on each machine, captures app, browser, idle, USB and print activity, encrypts and hash-chains it locally, and syncs it to a central axum + PostgreSQL server where an organisation's admins see their whole fleet. It started as a single-machine Windows tool and grew into a sellable product with self-serve org signup and per-seat trial licensing.
features: Native agents for Windows (Service), macOS (launchd) and Linux (systemd) from one Rust codebase — 62 tests green
Foreground app, window title, browser domain, idle time and scheduled screenshots
Exfiltration monitoring — files copied to USB, print jobs, USB device identity and installed transfer apps
Central org dashboard: fleet KPIs, cross-device timeline, transfers view, alert-rules editor and screenshot grid
Offline-first sync with retry and back-off; idempotent uploads keyed on ULIDs so retries never duplicate
Self-serve organisation signup, per-seat licensing with trial and expiry, OS-detecting download page
Privacy by design: no keylogging, credentials, cookies, webcam or microphone capture — ever

highlights.title: Tamper-evident by construction
highlights.body: Every event is SHA-256 hash-chained to the previous one and the chain travels with the data, so the server can independently re-verify each device. Retention purges re-seal the chain instead of leaving a break that looks like tampering.

highlights.title: Screenshots the server can't read
highlights.body: Each screenshot is encrypted on the device with AES-256-GCM, then re-encrypted under an org key before upload. The dashboard decrypts for that org only — the server operator never sees plaintext.

highlights.title: Session-0 split
highlights.body: A Windows service can't see the desktop, so a user-session collector writes encrypted blobs into a crash-safe, idempotent dropbox that the service ingests — keeping a single writer and a meaningful hash chain.

projects.title: Zero-Knowledge Vault
projects.status: Working build · security levels L1–L7 built
projects.context: Law-firm product for credentials and privileged documents
projects.desc: A local-first, zero-knowledge vault for passwords and documents — a Rust cryptographic core compiled to WebAssembly, encrypted sync that survives a malicious server, passkeys and guarded items.
projects.overview: A password and document vault where the server stores and syncs encrypted material but never holds the secret that unlocks it — and cannot lie about the vault's contents without being caught. All cryptography lives in a Rust core compiled to WebAssembly and run in a worker, so keys never touch the JavaScript heap. It ships as a web app, a browser extension and an Android shell, and works fully offline.
features: Passwords with folders, tags, custom fields, local search and an unbiased password generator
Documents up to 2 GiB, streamed and chunk-encrypted — filenames and metadata encrypted too
Encrypted multi-device sync protected against record swapping, rollback, silent deletion and forked histories
Guarded items whose keys are split so a second, biometric-confirmed device must approve every decryption
Client-generated recovery key, passkey (WebAuthn) sign-in, account 2FA and Postgres row-level security
Browser extension with sign-in, fill card and toolbar popup; installable web app; full offline CRUD

highlights.title: Built the attacker first
highlights.body: A 'lying server' harness can drop objects, replay old manifests, reorder deltas or show two devices different views. It was built before any defence and proven to succeed — then the signed Merkle manifest and AAD binding were added to make every attack fail.

highlights.title: Crypto frozen on day one
highlights.body: XChaCha20-Poly1305 with full AAD binding, Argon2id, Ed25519, X25519 and BLAKE3 from reviewed libraries, with #![forbid(unsafe_code)] — the on-disk format was fixed at the first level and never weakened.

highlights.title: Honest by construction
highlights.body: A ten-level build ladder ties each level to the class of data it may hold, and builds below the top level display a banner that cannot be switched off.

projects.title: KartIPR — IP Marketplace
projects.status: v1 live · v2 rebuild in progress
projects.desc: India's attorney-verified marketplace to buy, sell and license trademarks, patents, copyrights and designs — deal rooms, KYC, escrow-style payments and a separate team console.
projects.overview: A marketplace where owners list registered IP and buyers discover, negotiate and acquire it, with attorneys verifying ownership, registration status and litigation before anything goes live. The v2 rebuild splits the product into two Next.js apps — the public store and a team console — over a 54-model PostgreSQL schema, with a re-runnable migration that carries every v1 record across.
features: Eight kinds of IP — trademarks, patents, copyrights, designs and more — sold outright, licensed or co-developed
Attorney-verified listings, KYC, ownership checks and terms acceptance before a deal can start
Deal rooms with offers, messages, best-and-final rounds and an append-only deal-event history
Payments, payouts, invoices and a double-entry style ledger, with money handled in decimal.js — never floats
Valuation requests, appointments, memberships, support tickets and a conduct/strike policy in the schema
Separate store and admin console sharing code through a checked sync contract

highlights.title: Concurrency made explicit
highlights.body: Listing locks and queue claims mean two buyers can never open a deal on the same listing at once — interest is queued, not raced.

highlights.title: A smoke test for every route
highlights.body: One command requests every page and API route as a visitor, a buyer and a seller — exactly where a marketplace tends to leak.

highlights.title: Two apps, one set of rules
highlights.body: The store owns the schema and business rules; the console copies the files it needs via shared.json and warns on start if they drift. Shared modules never read either app's session.

projects.title: Visitor Management & SSO Identity
projects.desc: WhatsApp-driven visitor check-in for a law firm's reception that also became the single sign-on identity service for every internal product.
projects.overview: A visitor scans a QR code at reception, WhatsApp opens with a message ready to send, and the reply is a short-lived link to a registration form — pre-filled if they've visited before. Reception checks people in and out from the management portal. The same service owns the firm's staff accounts and mints the JWTs every other internal product trusts, which makes it the most load-bearing system the firm runs.
features: QR → WhatsApp → short link → pre-filled registration form, with no app to install
One person record per WhatsApp number and one row per visit — returning visitors never duplicate
Reception check-in, check-out and cancel, plus reception-entered visits from the portal
Shared staff identity: one account table, application-scoped JWTs, refresh tokens and super-admin user management
Five WhatsApp providers and two storage back-ends behind single interfaces — switching is a config change
Health endpoint, strict per-route rate limits and HMAC-verified webhooks

highlights.title: Phone numbers never in a URL
highlights.body: The visitor's number travels only inside a two-hour signed token behind a 16-character short code; the API only ever returns a masked value.

highlights.title: Strictly layered
highlights.body: Route → Zod validation → auth → application gate → controller → service → DAO. Express 5 forwards async errors, so controllers carry no try/catch and every response uses one envelope.

highlights.title: Fail loud at boot
highlights.body: One file may read process.env; it validates every variable with Zod and exits on a bad value, so a misconfigured deploy fails immediately instead of at the first request.

projects.title: Lead Recorder
projects.desc: A Flutter + Kotlin app that notices every lead call on its own, asks Save or Ignore after hang-up, and files the call and recording to a Fastify API with a Google Sheets mirror.
projects.overview: Leads were lost because calls happened and nobody wrote them down. Lead Recorder assumes nobody will: it detects the call itself and asks one question after hang-up — Save or Ignore. Android records through a Kotlin plugin; iOS, where apps can't record calls, uses a share extension for recordings made in the Phone app. Both land in the same Fastify + PostgreSQL backend, mirrored row by row into a Google Sheet.
features: Automatic call detection with a Save / Ignore notification seconds after hang-up
Smart recording choice — prefers the dialer's two-sided recording, respects manual start/pause/stop
Recent tab to catch up on the last 7 days of calls with Save all — safe to press twice
Indian numbers normalised to +91 and unknown callers named from the dialer's file name, server-side
Admin and user roles, Google Sheet mirror that can never block a save, 15-minute signed playback links
CI/CD: backend tested then deployed; signed APK published so phones offer 'Update available'

highlights.title: Idempotent by design
highlights.body: Calls are deduplicated on number + start time and on a client-supplied ID, so retries and 'Save all' can never store a call twice.

highlights.title: Hardened on both ends
highlights.body: bcrypt cost 12 with timing-safe unknown-email handling, pinned-algorithm JWTs, per-IP rate limits; on the phone the token is encrypted with an AES-256 key in the hardware keystore.

highlights.title: Rules live on the server
highlights.body: Number and name normalisation run in the API, so a backfill script can fix every old row when a rule changes.

projects.title: Blutec Ping
projects.desc: Optimized backend for a bulk WhatsApp messaging service. Integrated the WhatsApp API for high-volume queues and streamlined queries for large-scale broadcasts.
projects.overview: Ping by Blutec is a production WhatsApp marketing platform built on the official WhatsApp Business API — broadcast to thousands, let AI answer the replies, and surface the leads worth calling. I optimized the bulk-messaging backend and high-volume send queues so campaigns of 10,000+ contacts deliver reliably under WhatsApp's rate limits.
features: Bulk broadcasts to 10,000+ contacts per campaign with rate limits handled automatically
AI chatbots that answer incoming replies in seconds, around the clock
Lead and engagement scoring that routes qualified contacts to the sales team
Shared team inbox with agent assignment and internal notes
Approved-template campaigns with audience segmentation and personalisation variables
Delivery, read, reply and click analytics for every campaign

projects.title: Management Portal
projects.desc: One sign-in console for every internal product — a static React SPA that talks directly to each product's admin API, with data-driven modules, permissions and live health tiles.
projects.overview: Staff sign in once and work across every internal backend that's deployed, instead of keeping a password per tool. The portal owns no backend and no database: it is a static single-page app whose every screen is a view onto another product's admin API. Adding a new product is three small edits — a catalogue entry, an API service and a module folder — not a new application.
features: Sidebar, launcher, command palette and dashboard tiles all generated from one software catalogue
Visitor-management module: overview, visits, visitors, check-in actions and reorderable master lists
Website module: leads, newsletter subscribers, vacancies, job applications and a live careers form builder
Role- and application-based permissions with wildcards, enforced on routes and in the UI
Live health probe per backend — operational, degraded, offline or not deployed
CI on staging; deploy on main with an empty-build guard, rollback copy and health gate

highlights.title: One Axios client per backend
highlights.body: A lazy factory attaches the bearer token, unwraps the response envelope, normalises every error and shares a single transparent token refresh across concurrent requests.

highlights.title: Never invent data
highlights.body: There's no mock layer — a product with no backend shows 'Not configured', and the health sweep is scoped to the user's grants and shared across components for 15 seconds.

highlights.title: Kept out of search
highlights.body: robots.txt, a noindex meta tag and an X-Robots-Tag header keep an internal tool unindexable, including by AI crawlers.

projects.title: Hearing Alert — Docket Radar
projects.desc: Zero-fail patent deadline and hearing management — a statutory rules engine for IN, US, EP and PCT, an alert scheduler over email and WhatsApp, and OCR that reads official receipts.
projects.overview: In IP practice a missed statutory deadline can end a client's rights. Hearing Alert encodes those deadlines instead of remembering them: prosecution events across four jurisdictions and eight stages generate dated obligations, a scheduler decides when to alert, and OCR pulls dates and reference numbers out of official correspondence so a paralegal confirms a date instead of typing one.
features: Statutory rules engine for India, USPTO, EPO and WIPO/PCT across eight prosecution stages
Board, Kanban and calendar views with urgency tiers from 'safe' to 'overdue'
Deadline calculator — ask 'if the FER issued on this date, when is the response due?' without creating a matter
Three alert schedules (eve-of, halving, daily) over email and WhatsApp, with hearing-time reminders
Receipt upload with OCR and PDF parsing to extract reference numbers, fees and transaction dates
Firms, teams, clients, matters, roles and a per-firm audit log

highlights.title: Statutory vs extended vs verified
highlights.body: The rule's date, an obtained extension and a human verification are three separate things in the schema — 'waiting verification' is a first-class state, not a flag.

highlights.title: When decoupled from what
highlights.body: The alert schedule decides which days fire and the notification decides what it says, so either can change without the other.

highlights.title: Honest delivery
highlights.body: Without mail credentials, alerts are recorded as undelivered rather than silently marked as sent.

projects.title: L — Offline Voice Assistant
projects.desc: A Windows voice assistant with a fully local speech pipeline that opens apps, operates windows, sets reminders, speaks Hinglish — and hands harder tasks to Claude Code running headless.
projects.overview: Say 'Hey L' and an offline speech pipeline — wake word, voice-activity endpointing, Whisper transcription and Piper speech — turns the request into an intent. Plain rules handle everything they can: opening apps and sites, web searches, volume, media, reminders. Only the remainder reaches a model, through Claude Code in a small, fast 'ask' mode or a 'desktop' mode with lean custom tools for operating application windows.
features: Wake word, push-to-talk or off — switchable from the tray; push mode keeps Bluetooth earbuds out of headset mode
Local speech in and out: openWakeWord, faster-whisper, WebRTC VAD and Piper — nothing sent off to be transcribed
Rule-based router that understands English and Hinglish and replies in Hindi when spoken to in Hindi
Opens apps and sites, searches YouTube, GitHub, Maps and more, and pastes tasks into focused windows
Reminders, long-term memory and a name-aware greeting that never guesses a title
Autostart with a tray icon and a small web-view UI

highlights.title: Token-cost architecture
highlights.body: Rules first, a small model next, tools only when needed. A custom MCP server replaced a generic desktop tool whose screenshots cost hundreds of thousands of tokens per task — it returns short text lists of a single window's controls instead.

highlights.title: Deliberate blast radius
highlights.body: A voice-triggered agent gets no shell, registry or file-deletion tool, runs without the user's plugins or hooks, and may write only inside its own working folder.

highlights.title: Clicks without the mouse
highlights.body: Desktop actions use UI Automation 'invoke' wherever possible, so the cursor doesn't move while you work.

projects.title: EVA — Multilingual AI Assistant
projects.desc: A streaming AI chat assistant for a law-firm website, built into a Next.js redesign prototype with 3D visuals, an MDX journal and three explored design themes.
projects.overview: A next-generation take on the firm's public website, built to explore what the live site doesn't have yet. Its centrepiece is EVA, a chat assistant that streams Claude's replies from a server-side route so the system prompt and API key never reach the browser. Around it sit React Three Fiber visuals, an MDX-powered journal and three design directions backed by a documented reference teardown.
features: Streaming chat endpoint — the browser only ever sees EVA's words
Script pinning: detects Gujarati and Devanagari in the visitor's message and forces the reply into the same script
Config-gated integrations — EVA, booking, live chat and payments render nothing until configured
MDX journal with front matter, plus Zod-validated server actions for forms
3D hero visuals with React Three Fiber and drei
Three design themes explored on separate branches, with a token system per theme

highlights.title: Don't trust the model to guess the script
highlights.body: Smaller models often answer romanised Hindi or Gujarati in native script. The route detects the script deterministically from Unicode ranges and appends a hard directive.

highlights.title: Safe to half-configure
highlights.body: The endpoint returns 503 until its key is set, so a half-configured widget can never ship.

projects.title: Soni & Soni Website
projects.desc: A law-firm website and lead-management system with enquiry workflows and an admin panel that help clients connect with the firm directly.
projects.overview: A production website and lead-management platform for Soni & Soni, an Ahmedabad IP & trademark law firm that serves clients in 111+ countries. The site presents the firm's practice areas, global reach and credibility, and routes every enquiry into an internal lead system — backed by automation workflows that connect prospective clients with the right team member fast.
features: Marketing site for IP services — patent, trademark, copyright, design, startup and company registration
Lead-capture and enquiry workflows feeding an internal lead-management system
Admin panel for the team to manage enquiries and site content
Credibility sections — 25,000+ marks registered, 30,000+ clients, 111+ countries, testimonials
Fast, responsive Next.js frontend with 'Schedule a Consultation' conversion flows
Automation that routes incoming leads to the right team member

projects.title: Call Recorder
projects.desc: A privacy-maximal Android call recorder — no account, no server and no internet permission, so recordings physically cannot leave the phone.
projects.overview: The same capture engine as Lead Recorder with every network path removed. It records calls automatically, labels each recording from the call log and keeps everything in the app's private folder. The manifest declares no internet permission and Android backup is disabled — not 'we choose not to upload', but 'the OS won't let it'.
features: Starts recording when a call connects and stops at hang-up, with Pause / Resume / Stop in the notification
Labels each file with number, contact, direction and duration in a sidecar JSON
Deletes recordings of unanswered outgoing calls and boosts quiet audio automatically
Recordings grouped by day with search, incoming/outgoing filter, playback and delete
One-screen setup for permissions, the accessibility switch and auto-record
Only five direct dependencies — no network, analytics or storage-permission packages anywhere

highlights.title: No database by design
highlights.body: Each recording is a media file plus a JSON file beside it, so delete is genuinely destructive and the data is self-describing if it's ever copied off the phone.

highlights.title: Accessibility service that reads nothing
highlights.body: It exists only to unlock the microphone during calls and declares itself as not an assistive tool.

projects.title: Docket Watchdog
projects.desc: An IP-law operations platform that watches a firm's matter register, calculates deadline urgency, drafts reminders with Mistral and escalates — with a human in the loop at every external touchpoint.
projects.overview: Upload the firm's matter register as a CSV and Docket Watchdog keeps watching it: deterministic Python engines compute deadlines, priority and escalation, a scheduler re-runs them, and Mistral writes reminder drafts — but nothing goes out without a human approving it. A FastAPI backend serves a Streamlit dashboard over Neon PostgreSQL.
features: CSV matter-register upload with validation; dashboards always reflect the latest upload
Deterministic deadline, priority and escalation engines — AI is used only for drafting
Critical-matter and escalation queues with acknowledgement
Mistral-generated reminder drafts rendered through Jinja2 email templates
Scheduled re-evaluation with APScheduler and a full audit log
Typed with Pydantic v2 and covered by pytest

projects.title: AI-Powered OCR Pipeline
projects.desc: Converts unstructured PDFs and itineraries into database-ready JSON. Combines OpenAI, Mistral AI, AWS, Azure, MinerU and OCR, syncing to Directus — cutting manual entry 80%+.
projects.overview: A multi-format document-analysis engine that benchmarks cloud OCR services on real documents — PDFs, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, CSV and plain text — then scores extraction quality and maps exactly where each engine fails. Built as a production proof-of-concept at 7Span to choose the most accurate, lowest-cost OCR stack for automating manual data entry.
features: Dual-engine comparison — Azure Document Intelligence vs MinerU Cloud on identical inputs
Multi-format parsing (PDF, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, CSV, TXT) with automatic format detection
Document-structure detection: multi-column reordering, invoice grouping, table preservation
Accuracy metrics — similarity %, character/word accuracy, CER and WER (Levenshtein)
Character and word confusion maps that show precisely how each engine misreads
Dual-format baseline output (TXT + Markdown) plus structured JSON reports per document

projects.title: Instant Dukaan
projects.desc: A scalable SaaS empowering local shops to deploy custom storefronts. Responsive frontend plus robust APIs for fast onboarding and multi-tenant operations.
projects.overview: A multi-tenant SaaS that lets local retail shops launch their own online storefront quickly, without hiring a developer. I worked on the responsive storefront frontend and the APIs behind shop onboarding and day-to-day multi-tenant operations.
features: Self-serve onboarding so a local shop can go from sign-up to live storefront fast
Custom storefront per shop on shared multi-tenant infrastructure
Responsive React storefront built mobile-first for shoppers on phones
Express + MySQL APIs for shops, catalogue and orders
Tenant-scoped data so every shop sees only its own catalogue and orders

projects.title: Scout
projects.desc: A Google Maps B2B lead-generation tool streamlining automated business-data extraction, prospect discovery and client outreach.
projects.overview: A B2B lead-generation tool built on Google Maps data. Sales teams search by business type and location, Scout extracts structured business details at scale, and the results feed straight into prospecting and outreach — replacing hours of manual copy-paste research.
features: Search businesses by category and location on Google Maps
Automated extraction of structured business data into exportable lead lists
Prospect discovery to build targeted outreach lists fast
Built to feed client outreach workflows directly

projects.title: Enterprise ETL & Denormalization
projects.desc: Merged 30+ tables across 8-10 databases and 15M+ records into one source of truth. A Python ETL syncs daily inserts and improved retrieval ~60%.
projects.overview: Business data was spread across 8–10 databases and 30+ tables holding 15M+ records, so every report needed slow, resource-heavy multi-join queries. I designed a single denormalized master table as one source of truth and a Python ETL that keeps it in sync with daily inserts — improving data retrieval by roughly 60%.
features: Consolidated 30+ tables across 8–10 databases into one architecture
Centralized master-data table that removed expensive multi-join queries
Python ETL that syncs daily inserts into the master table
Around 60% faster data retrieval for reporting and operations
Handles 15M+ records

projects.title: Mahendra Ke Namkeen
projects.desc: A B2C eCommerce platform with optimized storefront and admin panel. Razorpay, secure auth, live orders and analytics for real revenue.
projects.overview: A B2C eCommerce platform for Mahendra Ke Namkeen, an Indore snack brand dating back to 1957. I built an optimized storefront and an admin panel with Razorpay payments, secure authentication, live order tracking and sales analytics, handling real customer revenue.
features: Product catalogue across the brand's namkeen ranges with cart and checkout
Razorpay payment integration for secure online payments
Secure customer authentication and order history
Admin panel for products, live orders and sales analytics
Optimized, responsive storefront for fast loads on mobile

projects.title: Multi-Model Content Automation
projects.desc: A task-handoff pipeline orchestrating Storyteller, Architect and Editor LLM roles, enforcing GEO and human-touch formatting without manual prompting.
projects.overview: An LLM task-handoff pipeline that splits content creation across three specialised roles — Storyteller, Architect and Editor — so each model does one job well. The chain enforces GEO (generative-engine optimization) structure and a human-touch formatting pass automatically, removing the manual prompt-chaining between steps.
features: Three-role LLM orchestration — Storyteller drafts, Architect structures, Editor refines
Automatic GEO formatting so output is tuned for AI answer engines
Human-touch pass that strips the robotic tone from generated copy
Zero manual prompt-chaining — each role hands off to the next programmatically
Delivered as a reproducible Jupyter pipeline

projects.title: Generative AI Fine-Tuning
projects.desc: Fine-tuned Meta Llama 3.1 8B with Unsloth and QLoRA on dual T4 GPUs. Built an ingestion pipeline over 40,000+ MongoDB articles for content generation.
projects.overview: Fine-tuned Meta's Llama 3.1 8B for domain content generation on a budget: Unsloth and QLoRA made it trainable on dual T4 GPUs, and a custom ingestion pipeline turned 40,000+ articles stored in MongoDB into a clean training set.
features: Llama 3.1 8B fine-tuned with Unsloth and 4-bit QLoRA
Trained on dual NVIDIA T4 GPUs — no expensive hardware needed
Ingestion pipeline over 40,000+ MongoDB articles to build the training set
Delivered as reproducible Jupyter notebooks

projects.title: X AI Automation Bot
projects.desc: A Python pipeline using free-tier LLM APIs to generate context-aware content and autonomously publish scheduled posts to X.
projects.overview: An autonomous social bot that generates context-aware posts with free-tier LLMs and publishes them to X on a schedule — no paid API tier required. Several model backends (Google Gemini, Mistral AI, OpenRouter) are wired in so it keeps running even when one free quota runs dry.
features: Context-aware post generation from a maintained topic/queue file
Multi-backend LLMs — Google Gemini, Mistral AI and OpenRouter, all free-tier
Autonomous scheduled publishing to X via the X API
Provider fallback so a single rate-limit never stops the pipeline
Pure-Python, lightweight and self-hostable

projects.title: Inshorts News Scraper
projects.desc: Scrapes daily trending domain-specific news from Inshorts and organizes it via Google Sheets API every morning — saving 2+ research hours a day.
projects.overview: A Python automation that scrapes trending, domain-specific news from Inshorts every morning and files it straight into Google Sheets — turning a daily 2+ hour manual research routine into a scheduled, hands-off job.
features: Scrapes category-specific trending news from Inshorts on a daily schedule
BeautifulSoup + Selenium handling for dynamically rendered content
Writes clean, structured rows to Google Sheets via the Sheets API
Runs every morning unattended — saves 2+ research hours a day
Single-file, low-dependency script that is easy to redeploy

projects.title: Task Management System
projects.desc: A co-developed MERN task-management system to isolate and streamline project workflows across multiple teams.
projects.overview: A MERN task-management system co-developed to keep project work separated and on track across multiple teams — each team gets its own isolated workspace for tasks, assignments and progress.
features: Team-isolated workspaces so projects don't bleed into each other
Task creation, assignment and status tracking
React frontend with an Express + MongoDB API
Designed for multiple teams working in parallel

projects.title: HTML Email Templates & Signatures
projects.desc: A table-based trademark-opposition notice template and branded email signatures with multiple working links that survive Gmail — hand-built HTML served from Cloudinary.
projects.overview: Email HTML is not web HTML. These deliverables — a trademark opposition notice rebuilt from an Illustrator export, and a set of personal email signatures — were built around what actually survives Gmail and Outlook. Each one is fully self-contained with relative paths only, so any single folder can ship on its own.
features: Opposition notice rebuilt as a table-based email with real, selectable HTML text instead of an embedded SVG
Banner signatures with up to 11 working links and no image map
Shared Python build that slices a banner into real <a> link regions measured from each person's artwork
Assets served from a single Cloudinary upload per signature

highlights.title: No image maps
highlights.body: Gmail strips image maps, so each link region is cut out of the banner and wrapped in its own anchor — more markup, but it actually works.

projects.title: Developer Portfolio
projects.desc: A responsive personal portfolio presenting development, data-engineering and AI work through a structured, JSON-driven content system.
projects.overview: This site. A fully JSON-driven personal portfolio built on the latest Next.js, presenting full-stack, data-engineering and AI work through one structured content system — edit the data and the whole site updates. Hand-built neo-brutalist design with a pure-CSS dark mode and generated social images.
features: Next.js 16 (App Router, Turbopack) + React 19 + TypeScript strict
Tailwind CSS v4 with a token-driven neo-brutalist design system
Single JSON content layer — every page and section reads from src/data
Pure-CSS dark mode via data-theme tokens, with no flash on load
Auto-generated Open Graph / Twitter social images using next/og
Per-page SEO metadata, sitemap, robots and JSON-LD Person schema
